notes.detailedSummary: The original arbitrary-field, arbitrary-dimensional, actual ample-bundle problem remains unchanged. Only O217, D214, N220, T171, Q222, and C218, including their clarifications, are mathematical prerequisites. All six extracted grant files match their supplied review-source hashes. notes.text:
Retain every complete characteristic-zero, residue-characteristic-zero, real-valued non-Archimedean field K, including trivial, discrete, nondiscrete, and non-algebraically-closed cases; a smooth geometrically integral projective X of arbitrary dimension n; its actual ample rational line bundle L; arbitrary Radon support; and raw mass V=(L^n). Metrics are actual all-point decreasing Fubini–Study net endpoints, including literal pole values. P16.3, P16.5, and P16.7 remain separate.

For a continuous psh reference ψ, E(u) initially equals (n+1)^(-1) times the sum, for j=0,...,n, of integral u MA(u^[j],0^[n-j]). Extended E(u) is the infimum of energies of continuous actual psh majorants. E1 consists of actual endpoints with E(u)>−∞. For a positive Radon measure μ of mass V, J(μ)=sup over continuous actual psh v of E(v)−integral v dμ. Constants cancel through E(v+c)=E(v)+cV.

O grants the genuine positive mixed E1 operator, raw mass, all-test integrability against outputs, weighted decreasing continuity for directed nets, extended decreasing-energy continuity, concavity, admissible affine curvature calculus, segment differentiation, reference covariance, and complete-field pushforward. Its normalization clarification is retained. It grants no general equation existence.

D grants invariant actual descent through the completed algebraic closure, extended energy equality, the invariant Radon lift, and continuous-dual equality. It does not descend arbitrary noninvariant singular tests or establish equation existence. N requires an already actual continuous single-atom norming reference and gives coercivity, not attainment. T supplies the actual ample equation and every-solution all-point uniqueness over trivial fields. Q supplies the split projective-line equation and local disk geometry. C supplies strict locality and comparison. None is silently strengthened.

The complete bodies and clarifications are preserved in sources/grant-O.tex, grant-D.tex, grant-N.tex, grant-T.tex, grant-Q.tex, grant-C.tex and their clarification files. All six file hashes match the supplied review hashes. input.json preserves the entire input. The mathematical labels are not support IDs; this local note records their permitted scopes. No unreviewed native191 or ROOT observation is a seventh grant.

notes.summary: From O: finite continuous dual implies all-E1 integrability; all-E1 integrability is equivalent to a finite unit-energy bound without an anchor. Genuine outputs have finite dual and attain it. The general converse still needs a uniform reference bound.
notes.detailedSummary: The proof uses continuous Radon nets and an actual directed FS-majorant construction for a convex-series endpoint. The exact scaling estimate is B(tu)≤tA0(u)+n(n+1)t²B(u)/2. A proved uniform A0≤M0 would yield the intrinsic/dual equivalence and coercivity, but no general M0 or prescribed-target attainment is established.
notes.text:
Use the original domain, actual cone, and raw operator in n1. Normalize u∈E1 by sup u=0, and put B(u)=−E(u)≥0 and Iμ(u)=integral (−u)dμ. Let Uμ be the supremum of Iμ(u) over normalized actual E1 potentials with B(u)≤1.

First, a finite Radon measure λ on a compact Hausdorff space integrates directed increasing nonnegative continuous nets correctly: integral supα gα dλ=supα integral gα dλ. For each t, {sup gα>t} is the union of the directed open sets {gα>t}. Every compact subset has a finite subcover, contained in one stage by directedness. Inner regularity identifies the limiting open-set mass with the supremum of stage masses. For finitely many layer levels choose one common index; finite lower layer sums, followed by increasing height cutoffs, prove the integral identity. This does not assert monotone convergence for arbitrary measurable nets.

Suppose J(μ)<∞. For any actual u∈E1 choose continuous FS fα↓u and a tail bounded above by a constant M. The dual inequality gives
integral (M−fα)dμ ≤ MV+J(μ)−E(fα) ≤ MV+J(μ)−E(u).
The continuous Radon-net identity passes this finite bound to M−u. Thus every actual E1 potential is absolutely μ-integrable and its pole set has μ-mass zero. The same identity gives integral fα dμ→integral u dμ; O gives E(fα)↓E(u). Therefore each singular objective is the limit of its continuous objectives. The supremum over actual E1 equals J(μ).

Next, all-E1 integrability implies Uμ<∞ without a norming point. Otherwise choose normalized uj with B(uj)≤1 and Iμ(uj)≥4^j. Set vN=sum from j=1 to N of 2^(−j)uj, with the remaining coefficient 2^(−N) on the reference zero. O gives actual E1 vN, vN+1≤vN≤0, and E(vN)≥−1. Let v=infN vN. If v were identically −∞, for M>1/V the decreasing closed sets {vN≥−M} would have empty intersection. Compactness gives an empty member, so E(vN)≤E(−M)=−MV<−1, a contradiction.

Recognize v as an actual endpoint before asserting finite energy. Let F be the family of continuous weighted FS f satisfying f≥vN+ε for some N and ε>0. Defining FS approximants, followed by arbitrarily small constant additions, show that F is nonempty and inf F=v pointwise. It is downward directed: given f≥vN+ε and g≥vM+δ, take L≥N,M and 0<η<min(ε,δ)/4. Continuous FS hα↓vL eventually satisfy hα≤min(f,g)−2η everywhere, since the corresponding decreasing closed upper-level sets have empty intersection. Then hα+η belongs to F and lies below f,g. Hence F is an actual decreasing FS net to the nontrivial v. Every member has energy at least −1. O's extended decreasing-energy identity gives E(v)≥−1 before E1 membership is asserted. Thus v∈E1. Sequential monotone convergence yields Iμ(v)=sum 2^(−j)Iμ(uj)≥sum 2^j=∞, contradiction.

Conversely, Uμ<∞ implies all-E1 integrability. Concavity gives B(tu)≤tB(u). Take t=1 if B(u)≤1 and t=1/B(u) otherwise. Then tu remains normalized, has cost at most one, and tIμ(u)≤Uμ. Therefore Iμ(u)≤Uμ max(1,B(u)). Finite constant shifts handle all other potentials. This linear estimate alone does not prove J finite.

There is a sharper exact scaling estimate with the reference term exposed. Define Ak(u)=integral (−u)MA(u^[k],0^[n−k]), k=0,...,n. O makes these finite nonnegative numbers, with B=(sum Ak)/(n+1). For 0<t≤1, affine curvature and the genuine energy identity give
B(tu)=t/(n+1) sum over j=0,...,n and k=0,...,j of binomial(j,k)t^k(1−t)^(j−k)Ak.
The k=0 contribution is at most tA0. For k≥1 use Ak≤(n+1)B and sum of the corresponding binomial weights 1−(1−t)^j≤jt. Thus
B(tu)≤tA0(u)+Cn t²B(u), where Cn=n(n+1)/2.
At t=0 use the reference directly, without multiplying a pole value by zero.

Conditional conclusion: if a finite M0 has independently been proved with A0(u)≤M0 for every normalized actual E1 potential, set c=2(M0+1+sqrt(Cn)) and t=1/[c(1+sqrt(B(u)))]. Then B(tu)≤3/4, and Iμ(u)≤A(1+sqrt(B(u))), where A=cUμ. Consequently the objective is at most −B+A(1+sqrt B), and J≤A+A²/4. Together with the preceding results, this proves equivalence of intrinsic integrability, finite Uμ, and finite J under that additional reference bound. It proves coercivity, not attainment. General M0 remains unproved here.

An unconditional necessary-target statement is available for already genuine outputs. If μ=MA(w), w∈E1, O integrates all tests against μ. Concavity and the actual segment derivative give E(v)−E(w)≤integral (v−w)dμ for every actual v∈E1. All integrals are evaluated on a common finite-value full-measure set. Therefore every objective is bounded by the finite number E(w)−integral w dμ. Continuous majorants of w converge in energy and in their integrals against this fixed output by O's weighted law. Hence J(μ)=E(w)−integral w dμ, attained by w. This does not produce a solution for a prescribed intrinsic target.

notes.summary: Actual incidence points over one common complete coefficient-Gauss field preserve every original section value. Explicit residual-coordinate and cohomological hypotheses remain; the general Shilov bound is not proved.
notes.detailedSummary: A residual Jacobian argument proves independence of the full hyperplane coefficient set, including solved constants. Under explicit initial point hypotheses and negative-twist vanishing (H), the construction gives a smooth geometrically integral actual curve of raw degree m^(n−1)V, actual points with completed residue field H_i(A_free)^, and residual degree one. Algebraic-closure lifts are constructed directly. No application of GM A.7 to a transcendental extension is made.
notes.text:
Let C be complete algebraically closed, nontrivially valued, with characteristic and residue characteristic zero. Let X/C be smooth geometrically integral projective of dimension n≥2, and choose an actual very ample M=mL after clearing rational denominators. An embedding is given by S0,...,SN. Put gl=Sl/S0 on S0≠0.

Assume finitely many actual points yi have generic scheme support, |gl(yi)|≤1, and that their coordinate reductions generate a subfield k(Yi) of transcendence degree n over k=the residue field of C. These reductions are affine coordinates of an integral k-variety Yi. Also assume trdeg over k of the residue field of Hi=H(yi) is n. Equality of this residue field with k(Yi) is unnecessary. These hypotheses have not been established here for every required reference Shilov point.

Put s=n−1, r′=sN, and r=s(N+1). Over each Hi form the unit-radius Gauss extension in free variables Ajl, j=1,...,s and l=1,...,N, and complete it to H′i. Solve Aj0=−sum_l Ajl gl(yi).

All r full coefficient residues are independent over k. Indeed consider Yi×A^(r′)→A^r, retaining all free coordinates and outputting the s solved constants. At a smooth residual point, the embedding-coordinate differentials span the n-dimensional cotangent space. Choose s independent coefficient rows. The differential has an identity block of size r′ and an additional rank-s block in the Yi directions. An r-minor is nonzero, hence remains nonzero at the generic point. In characteristic zero, independent differentials imply algebraic independence: the differential rank of a subfield equals its transcendence degree, by a transcendence basis and separability. Thus the incidence projection is dominant, proving independence in k(Yi)(A_free), and therefore in the larger residue field of H′i.

Let F be the completion of C(A_all) with the coefficient-Gauss norm on all r independent symbols. This same F embeds isometrically in every H′i. For a nonzero polynomial in the full coefficients, divide by a C-coefficient of maximal norm. Its residual polynomial is nonzero and cannot vanish on the independent residues. Evaluation therefore has exactly its coefficient-Gauss norm. Fractions preserve quotient norms, giving an injective isometric map; completeness extends it to F. Different representations of the solved coefficients at different yi do not change the domain field. Completion changes neither value group nor residue field, since a sufficiently close approximation preserves the norm and unit residue. Thus the residue of F is k(A_all), and that of H′i is residue(Hi)(A_free).

For an independent geometric-integrality proof impose the explicit finite cohomological premise (H): H^q(X,O_X(−kM))=0 for 1≤k≤n−1 and 1≤q≤n−1. Availability of sufficiently high powers follows by classical Serre duality and vanishing, whose recursive proofs are not newly supplied here; (H) remains an explicit premise of this formulation.

The n−1 full generic hyperplanes Aj0 S0+sum_l Ajl Sl=0 cut out an actual smooth geometrically integral projective curve D over F. Work first over E=C(A_all). For a smooth embedded projective variety of dimension d, vanishing of a hyperplane section and its differential at a specified point imposes d+1 independent linear conditions, because the embedding coordinates span the cotangent space. The bad-pair incidence has dimension N−1, whereas hyperplane parameter space has dimension N; its projection is closed by projectivity. It misses the generic hyperplane, including after algebraic closure. Iterate with the independent coefficient rows. Each intersection is smooth of expected dimension and the next equation is nonzero on every component. Projective intersection dimension ensures nonemptiness in the dimensions used. The equations form a regular sequence.

Its Koszul resolution has terms O_X(−kM) in degree −k. In degree-zero hypercohomology, H^k and H^(k−1) of these terms vanish by (H), with H^0 of negative ample twists zero. Hence H^0(D_E,O)=E. Finite affine Čech covers of separated schemes have affine intersections, and tensoring their complexes with a field is exact; the assertion persists over algebraic closures and over F. A smooth geometric curve has disjoint irreducible components. More than one would give a nontrivial global idempotent, contradicting this global-functions equality. Thus D is geometrically integral. Its actual restricted L has degree deg(L|D)=m^(n−1)(L^n), since the actual regular-sequence intersection class is M^(n−1). No numerical replacement bundle is used.

The evaluations F[gl]→H′i annihilate the hyperplane equations and define an actual analytic point y′i of D. Its projection to X is exactly yi. Prove generic support before using a function-field injection: its seminorm residue contains k(Yi)(A_free), of transcendence degree n+r′ over k, and the base residue k(A_all), of degree r′+n−1. Thus its residual transcendence degree over F is at least one. A nongeneric point of an integral F-curve is closed and has finite residue extension of F; its valuation residue is algebraic. The latter follows because lifts of any residue-linearly-independent set are linearly independent over the base field, after normalizing a relation by a maximal coefficient. This contradiction establishes generic support and injection of F(D).

The image of F(D) contains C(X) and all free variables. C(X) is dense in Hi because yi has generic support. Finite coefficient approximation gives Gauss-density of C(X)(A_free) in Hi(A_free); a sufficiently accurate nonzero denominator approximation preserves its norm and controls its inverse. Therefore H(y′i)=H′i. Its residual transcendence degree over F is exactly (n+r′)−(r′+n−1)=1.

There is no new value group. For completeness, units with d independent residues and elements with q rationally independent values modulo the base group are algebraically independent: group a polynomial by exponents of the latter elements; independent unit residues determine each coefficient-polynomial norm, and different groups have distinct valuations, so a least-valuation term survives. Thus d+q≤n in C(X). Taking d=n shows the value-group extension is torsion. Since C has divisible value group inside R, a torsion extension has no new value: divide an integer multiple in the group by that integer. Unit Gauss extension and completion preserve the group. All original rational-function evaluations are isometric; expressing any original section in a rational frame proves preservation of its norm in every pulled-back continuous metric.

Actual algebraic-closure lifts are also available. Put B=completed algebraic closure of F. Extend F→H′i to algebraic closures, using uniqueness of the valuation extension from complete F, and complete inside Ωi=completed algebraic closure of H′i. The resulting B-coordinate evaluations define zi on D_B. The old injected F(D) survives, so H′i embeds in H(zi). Residues of Ωi are algebraic over residue(H′i), and residue(B) is algebraic over residue(F); therefore zi retains relative residual degree one. The same closed-point argument proves generic support before invoking B(D). Its completed residue field is the closure of B(D) in Ωi. The value group remains the original divisible group. These are the usual type-II invariants. Actual semistable-model recognition still requires the audited curve geometry. GM A.7 is not applied to the initial transcendental extension F/C.

Limitations: initial actual Shilov-coordinate hypotheses, semistable containment of these lifts, domination of all already actual restricted metrics, the genuine raw curvature formula, and the uniform reference bound M0 remain unproved. This construction supplies neither a general intrinsic target criterion nor an equation theorem.

notes.summary: Positive graph interpolation is reconstructed with irrational cycles intact, using shared value-group values and two rational slopes per edge. It does not recognize an actual metric.
notes.detailedSummary: The theorem allows signed starting vertex curvature, positive real edge weights, lengths in a nonzero divisible subgroup, and any nonnegative vertex target of the same positive mass. Refined approximants have positive curvature at every vertex and converge uniformly, with weak curvature convergence. Exact checks cover the displayed prototype and 81 finite variants only.
notes.text:
Let Λ be a nonzero divisible subgroup of R, and G a finite connected metric graph with lengths in Λ and positive weights we. Let signed vertex measure θ and nonnegative vertex measure μ have the same mass V>0. For an anchor z there is a unique edge-affine F with F(z)=0 and θ+ΔF=μ, where Δ is weighted outgoing slope. It admits subdivisions and rational-slope approximants Gj with values in Λ at every vertex, one common denominator at each stage, uniformly converging to F, with θ+ΔGj≥0 and weakly converging to μ. Every refined vertex has strictly positive curvature at each stage.

Proof: subdivide self-loops at their Λ-valued midpoints, retaining the loops and adding zero initial masses. Edge cancellation gives −sum_v h(v)Δh(v)=sum_e we(h(b)−h(a))²/ℓe. The vertex matrix is symmetric and has exactly constants as kernel, so its image consists of zero-sum vectors. This proves anchored solvability. A singleton without edges is immediate.

Mix μ with ε(V/k) times the sum of all vertex atoms, where k is the vertex count. The resulting με has positive margins at every old vertex; its anchored solution Fε tends uniformly to F. Λ is dense since it contains Qa for any nonzero a∈Λ. Approximate the shared Fε vertex values by gv∈Λ, keeping gz=0. On an oriented edge put d=gb−ga and c=d/ℓ. Choose rational q1<c<q2 arbitrarily close to c and set t=(d−q2ℓ)/(q1−q2). Then 0<t<ℓ and t∈Λ. Use q1 on the first subedge and q2 on the second. The endpoint is exactly gb, and the bend value ga+q1t belongs to Λ. Shared endpoint values preserve every cycle exactly.

The bend atom is we(q2−q1)>0. Endpoint contributions are we q1 and −we q2. Make each slope error smaller than η, with η times the incident weight sum below half the old positive curvature margin. Every old vertex stays positive. Total Δ-mass remains zero. Uniform function error is bounded by the vertex error plus η times maximal edge length; inserted curvature mass tends to zero with η. Let these errors and ε tend to zero. Old masses converge to μ and the inserted masses disappear weakly. A common integer clears the finitely many rational slopes, preserving Λ-valued vertices.

Fixed-edge rational slopes cannot replace this construction: on parallel edges of lengths 1 and sqrt(2), a common difference with rational slopes belongs to Q intersect sqrt(2)Q={0}. For θ=(1,1), μ=(2,0), ε=1/10, d=(9/10)(2−sqrt(2)), rational slope pairs (52/100,53/100) and (37/100,38/100) give bends −127+90sqrt(2) and −180+128sqrt(2). Curvature masses are 189/100, 9/100, 1/100, 1/100, totaling exactly 2.

finite_checks.py verifies these identities and 81 specified variants using exact fractions and Q(sqrt(2)). Rerun with python3 finite_checks.py; output is finite-check-output.json. The general proof is in P16.4-argument.md. Neither the graph proof nor its finite checks constructs a formal model or actual psh metric.

notes.summary: Explicit node monomials prove vertical Cartier gluing and degree correction under an actual split cover. Whole mod-a vanishing/generation and actual generic section identification suffice for pure-FS recognition, but remain unverified generally.
notes.detailedSummary: The local overlap ratios are literal units, and normalized reductions give orders q and −q. The calculation avoids the analytic-meromorphic slope theorem only for these vertical monomials. Identical adic layers lift finitely many generators through every thickening. This does not establish the required global cover, whole nil-fibre ampleness, GAGA premises, or raw Monge–Ampère coefficient formula.
notes.text:
First lemma. Let R=C° for complete algebraically closed nontrivial C. Assume an actual proper split strict semistable formal curve has a node-and-vertex cover: an oriented node block is étale over Spf R⟨x,y⟩/(xy−π), of length val(π); its endpoints a,b have val(x)=0 and val(x)=val(π). On overlaps with the smooth vertex part at a, x is a formal unit; at b, y is a formal unit. Distinct node blocks meet through those smooth parts. Their reductions give the usual branch parameters without extra zeros or poles. Subdivide self-loops first, retaining both branches.

For an integral Λ-affine f with Λ-valued vertices choose cv with val(cv)=f(v). Use meromorphic equation gv=cv on a vertex block and ge=ca x^q on a node block where f=f(a)+q val(x), q∈Z. Flatness and xy=π make these non-zero-divisors; negative powers lie in the total meromorphic ring. All are invertible generically. On the a overlap ge/ga=x^q is a unit. On the b overlap ge/gb=(caπ^q/cb)y^(−q) is a unit, since val(caπ^q/cb)=0. Overlap ratios satisfy the cocycle identity in the common meromorphic ring. Thus they define an actual vertical Cartier divisor D, not merely an abstract function of norm one.

In the frame g^(−1) of O(D), the canonical generic section 1 has norm |g|; its additive weight is val(g)=f composed with the retraction. On component Ca normalize its rational section by 1/ca: its coefficient near the node is x^q, giving residual order q. At Cb the coefficient is a unit times y^(−q), giving order −q. On smooth vertex parts it is one. Summing rational-section orders on the proper residual components yields degree correction Δf(v), with the positive outgoing-slope convention. Edge corrections total zero. Tensoring an already actual formal bundle retains its actual generic bundle and adds these residual degrees. Clear a common denominator for rational slopes. This avoids an analytic-meromorphic slope extension for this vertical calculation only. It does not prove the cover theorem, global domination/algebraization, or the genuine raw analytic curvature coefficients.

Second lemma. Let 0<|a|<1, and let a proper flat separated a-adically complete formal R-curve have complete separated local rings. Suppose its generic carrier is identified with the original X analytification, and an actual formal invertible sheaf A is identified generically with the original actual dL. Assume some A^k modulo a is generated by finitely many global sections and H1(X0,A0^k)=0 on the whole mod-a fibre. Also assume generic global analytic sections coincide, under the given identification, with algebraic sections of the actual kdL.

Put Ar=A^k/a^(r+1)A^k. Flatness and invertibility give identical layers a^r A^k/a^(r+1)A^k≅A0^k and exact sequences 0→A0^k→Ar→Ar−1→0. The single H1 vanishing makes every global-section transition surjective. Lift the finitely many mod-a generators compatibly through all r. Completeness gives global formal sections. They generate formally: in a local frame write any coefficient modulo a as a combination of generator coefficients, subtract, divide the error by a, and repeat. The resulting coefficient series converge adically and give an exact expression, without Noetherianity.

The generic sections are algebraic by the stated premise and have no common zero. In a formal local frame their coefficients fi have |fi|≤1. An integral identity 1=sum bi fi with |bi|≤1 forces max_i|fi|=1 at every analytic point. Hence the formal metric equals the pure FS metric defined by precisely these algebraic sections with zero weights. Dividing by k and d retains the actual original rational bundle.

The hypotheses are not verified for every required semistable curve. In particular, positive degrees on the reduced residual components do not by themselves establish the stated whole mod-a cohomology premise. A concrete obstruction to a shortcut is that this nil thickening need not have nilpotent nilradical: with divisible dense group and val(a)=1 choose bN of value 1/(N+1). Its class modulo a is nilpotent, but bN^N is nonzero modulo a. Thus the nilradical has no uniform nilpotence exponent. A valid whole-fibre ampleness/vanishing argument or a verified descent replacement is still needed.

Full arguments are in P16.4-argument.md and P16.4-paper.tex. finite_checks.py checks 100 specified valuation inequalities illustrating the nilpotence statement; this is finite evidence only. These lemmas do not establish an unconditional all-genus equation.
